tagline: The old coast-to-coast road, Indiana line to the Mississippi.
intro: From the Indiana line the old coast-to-coast road comes across on US 30 through Frankfort and Joliet to Aurora, turns up the Fox River Valley on Illinois 31 to Geneva, and heads west on Illinois 38 into farm country. It passes through DeKalb, where Joseph Glidden patented the double-strand barbed wire still in common use, and goes on through Rochelle and Dixon to Fulton on the Mississippi.

The highway was dedicated in 1913, Times Square to San Francisco. Its association had little money for building road, so it sponsored short stretches of concrete to make the case, called seedling miles. The first official one was finished in November 1914, just west of Malta.

moments.title: Rochelle
moments.text: An old Standard Oil filling station is restored as a visitors center, and at Railroad Park people come from across the country to watch trains where two railroads cross.

moments.title: Franklin Grove
moments.text: The Lincoln Highway Association keeps its national headquarters here in a restored 1860 general store, built by Harry Isaac Lincoln, a cousin of Abraham's.

moments.title: Fulton
moments.text: The road ends at the Mississippi beside De Immigrant, a nine-story Dutch windmill by the levee, in a town that keeps Dutch Days the first weekend of May.
